title: Spin Relaxation and Electrical Control of Spin Transport in Few-Layer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$
authors: T. Wakamura, M. Hashisaka, M. Bard, S. Okazaki, T. Sasagawa, T. Taniguchi, K. Watanabe, K. Muraki, N. Kumada
abstract: We report electrical tuning of spin relaxation in atomically thin $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$, a representative low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenide. Weak antilocalization measurements reveal strong spin--orbit interaction with spin--orbit lengths of tens of nanometers, consistent with recent theoretical predictions. Despite the semimetallic nature of $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$, in the ultrathin limit the spin--orbit scattering time can be tuned electrostatically by up to threefold. We further investigate vertical electric field effects on the spin--orbit length and time, and demonstrate the modulation of the Rashba parameters. Relation between spin--orbit scattering time and the diffusion coefficient indicates that spin relaxation is governed by the D'yakonov--Perel' mechanism in both monolayer and bilayer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$. These results establish few-layer $T_{\rm d}$-MoTe$_2$ as a platform for electrically tunable spin transport, thereby providing insight into spin relaxation in low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenides.
summary: This work reports on the electrical control of spin transport in few-layer $T_{m d}$-MoTe$_2$ using magnetotransport measurements. By analyzing Weak Antilocalization signals, the authors demonstrated that the spin relaxation time can be tuned significantly by an external electric field. These findings establish the material as a promising platform for realizing tunable spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the electrical control of spin relaxation and spin transport in few-layer $T_{m d}$-MoTe$_2$, a low-symmetry transition metal dichalcogenide.
main_result: The researchers demonstrated that the spin relaxation time ($	au_{so}$) in few-layer $T_{m d}$-MoTe$_2$ can be electrostatically tuned by up to threefold, confirming that the D'yakonov–Perel' mechanism governs spin relaxation.
method: Low-temperature magnetotransport measurements, specifically Weak Antilocalization (WAL) measurements, were performed using dual-gate structures to probe spin-orbit interactions.
model_or_system: The physical system is few-layer $T_{m d}$-MoTe$_2$. The analysis relies on the Iordanskii, Lyanda-Geller, and Pikus (ILP) theoretical framework to fit the magnetoconductivity data and extract characteristic spin-orbit lengths and relaxation times.
key_observables: Spin-orbit length ($L_{so}$), spin relaxation time ($	au_{so}$), magnetoconductivity ($\Delta\sigma(B)$), and Rashba parameters.
important_parameters: The tunability of $	au_{so}$ by up to threefold via gate voltage, and the identification of the D'yakonov–Perel' mechanism.
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the ILP model, which is an approximation, and the study notes that contributions from topological channels were not explicitly included.
figures_summary: Figures show magnetoconductivity variations ($\Delta\sigma(B)$) at different temperatures and gate voltages, illustrating the gate-dependent modulation of $L_{\phi}$ and $	au_{so}$.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing the strong spin-orbit coupling via WAL measurements, quantifying the electrical tunability of spin relaxation, and confirming the underlying physical mechanism (DP mechanism) through theoretical fitting.
why_interesting: The ability to electrically tune spin relaxation in a 2D material like MoTe$_2$ is highly relevant for developing spintronic devices, which often rely on controlling spin lifetimes and transport mechanisms.

Figure 5 presents the ﬁts at diﬀerent r from r = 0 to r = 1000 for the samples with diﬀerent thicknesses and vertical electric ﬁelds. The obtained ﬁtting parameters and the residual sum of squares (RSS) for the condition shown in Fig. 5(a) are given in Table I as representative results. The inset of Fig. 5 shows the RSS as a function of r, which clearly shows that the better ﬁt is obtained in the limit of r →0 (Bso1 →0) and validates the analysis using Eq. (1).
